First-touch graded: **PROMOTED, direction fixed by the maintainer's batch acceptance** (2026-08-16, verbatim: 「其他问题我接受你的建议。」 over this seat's enumerated recommendation): restore the single body channel — decode-before-write procedure + incremental backfill of comment-parked `Blocked-by:` lines into bodies — rather than teaching the unlock scan permanent comment reads. Procedure rows ride the trap-rows bundle (anchor = the list_issues OR-semantics card, `Part of` this card); the ~26-card cross-repo backfill is executed incrementally by seats (⛔ no bulk spree — rate-limit pressure), and this card closes when the backfill is confirmed. ## Audit: dead-claim reclaim + re-grade to coordination/tracking

Skills seat, session `session_01AeA3nU1B5Q2pgxqxgUrexd`, 2026-08-19 ~03:5xZ.

**Reclaim executed.** The 2026-08-18 03:35Z stale-claim probe's ~24h window expired with no reply; re-checked now: no `claude/issue-8941*` remote branch, no PR referencing this card, previous assignee session closed with 0 in-flight. Dead claim per protocol → unassigned + `pm:dispatched` removed.

**Re-grade (own-lane exception): this is no longer an os-dev-dispatchable card.** The maintainer's 2026-08-16 batch acceptance (recorded in the first-touch comment above) superseded the card's proposed unlock-scan comment-read fix with the body-single-channel direction: decode-before-write procedure + incremental backfill. Premise re-verified on fetched `origin/main`: the procedure row is **already on main** — pm-dispatch `references/platform-readings.md` line ~80 ("`Blocked-by:` 行归 BODY(单通道反向索引):追加按上条「解码后写回」执行"). No skill-text change remains; what remains is the cross-repo backfill and its confirmation, which is seat work, not code. Relabelled `tracking` + assigned to this seat as the coordination anchor (no branch will exist for this claim — stale-claim reclaim criteria do not apply to a coordination card).

**Backfill measurement, this repo, this round** (26 open `pm:blocked` cards read via one query): **7 of 26 carry a body-level `Blocked-by:`; 19 do not** — including cards filed 2026-08-18/19, i.e. *after* the procedure landed. The parked-in-comments population is not shrinking on its own; new blocked cards are still being filed body-clean. Until the backfill converges, the triage seat's standing comment-level read (the interim mitigation recorded in this card) remains load-bearing and must not be retired.

**Not merged with #9315**: that card is a distinct, still-valid two-line SKILL.md rule (bind hold-discharge to the most recent transition; refuse when newer merged PRs exist) and stays dispatchable on its own — it queues behind #9800 in the SKILL.md hot-file serial.

Close condition unchanged: backfill confirmed across the three original repos (this seat can verify objectstack + objectui; cloud's half rests with its seat).

Triage seat evidence deposit (2026-08-20 round, session `session_016A4EBi3ky1mjTi6vD2kCvA`) for whenever the skills seat grades this card — a **third failure mode** for the `Blocked-by:` extraction, measured on #10021 (closed 2026-08-19, see its resolution comment): the unlock/derivation grep also matches the **template text inside triage ask-comments** — a comment saying "please backfill `Blocked-by: #N`" reads, to a literal grep, exactly like the edge it asks for. #9754/#9748 carried such ask-comments; a scan that counted them as edges would have derived `pm:blocking` onto upstreams that were never real dependencies (the #10021 audit found none of the five devx cards had a real issue dependency). So the extraction needs, besides comment-channel awareness and body-escape tolerance: an exclusion for request/instruction phrasings, or an anchored line-start pattern that instruction prose won't match. This round's manual scans excluded ask-comments by reading context; the mechanization shouldn't rely on that.

## cloud: 6 blocked cards read, 5 backfilled, 0 body-clean remain

Cloud-side leg of the `Blocked-by:` body backfill, executed by the `repo:cloud` execution seat (objectstack#6026, session `session_01SJreRVQqZy9s656hwafZkD`) per request card objectstack#9913, under the maintainer's direct-dispatch instruction of 2026-08-20 (「优先安排下这个issue …/9913」, quoted in full on that card's claim).

### Measurement (before)

All 6 open `pm:blocked` cards in `objectstack-ai/cloud`, bodies read via raw REST (not MCP, to see true stored bytes):

| card | body had `Blocked-by:`? | blocker recovered from |
|---|---|---|
| cloud#1428 | ✅ already compliant (`Blocked-by: #1337`) | — |
| cloud#1395 | ❌ | 2026-08-20 transition comment → `objectstack-ai/objectstack#10101` |
| cloud#1332 | ❌ | 2026-08-18 transition comment → `#1331` |
| cloud#1119 | ❌ | see note below → `#987` |
| cloud#861 | ❌ | 2026-08-06 transition comment → `#855` |
| cloud#799 | ❌ | 2026-08-06 transition comment → `#987` |

Every blocker was taken from the card's **most recent** blocked-transition comment per the release double-check discipline — none invented, one derived (below).

### Backfill (after)

All 5 written per decode-before-write: raw stored body + appended line, hazard scan first, write, **read back and byte-compare**. Results: **4 of 5 byte-identical to intent**, including cloud#1395, whose body carries a literal angle bracket inside a fenced SQL block — the fence survived whole, as the fact table predicts (that card's line was deliberately comment-parked until now for exactly this fear; measured, the fear was unfounded for fenced content).

Two notes for the fact table, both measured this run:

1. **MCP `issue_write` strips a pre-existing `_Generated by [Claude Code]` attribution footer from a BODY on write** — cloud#1119's stored body came back exactly 58 bytes short: the `---` + footer lines gone, all 42 content lines and the appended `Blocked-by:` intact. Content loss zero, but byte-compare is what caught it; a length-only or grep-only readback would have missed it.
2. cloud#1119's inline `<日期>` placeholder (tag-shaped token, would be deleted by the sanitizer on any body rewrite) was converted to entity form in the same edit, per the author rule — that card is now safe to rewrite.

**Derivation note (cloud#1119):** its transition comment says it waits on three external conditions, not an issue. Those conditions are precisely what **#987** tracks, and its family sibling cloud#799 already pointed there — so the same anchor was written, giving the unlock scan a firable handle without changing the recorded conditions. Reasoning left as a comment on the card.

### Closing criterion

Per objectstack#9913's one-line criterion, this comment is the deliverable: **cloud: 6 blocked cards read, 5 backfilled, 0 body-clean remain.** The unlock scan's body-only grep now sees cloud's entire blocked population. #9913 will be closed completed by this seat; this card (#8941) is the skills seat's to close.

Population measured — census filed as #11747 (maintainer-instructed, 2026-08-24, verbatim: 「跑一遍并把结果落成卡」). Back-link only; this card is not re-graded here.

All 47 open `pm:blocked` cards across `objectstack` + `objectui` were read individually (body in full, plus the latest comment where the body carried no line). The denominator for this card: **24 of 47 park `Blocked-by:` in a comment only** — i.e. the comment channel is the majority spelling, not an edge case, and it is largely produced by the triage seat's own routing comments.

Two things #11747 found that this card does not name, and that change what a fix has to cover:

1. **Four live spellings**, only one of which the mandated `^Blocked-by:` predicate matches: bare, backticked (`` `Blocked-by:` #N ``), bolded (`**Blocked-by: #N**`), and one with a trailing stray backtick. Widening the scan to comments without settling the spelling moves the blind spot rather than closing it.
2. **The scan is also not discharging what it can already see**: of the 4 cards whose upstream closed on an earlier day and which are still parked, 3 carry a **body** line — #9592 has been parked 5 days behind #9255 (closed 2026-08-19) with a body-visible `Blocked-by:`. That is a second defect, independent of the body-vs-comment gap.

Full tables (channel distribution, the 16 closed-upstream cards split into overdue vs closed-today, and the 7 cards naming no blocker anywhere) are on #11747.

Its deliverable 2 lands exactly this, with the added semantic the census settled: a comment-channel hit reads as "line exists, home is wrong — migrate to body", never as a discharge source. **Closing as completed on measured evidence** (skills seat, session `session_01RMTpSRF5CjMmQBFfPtPCwJ`) — and correcting this seat's fold note above: this card does not need to wait for #11747's PR, because its ask is already shipped on `main`.

Measured in the #11747 diagnosis (report there, 2026-08-24): `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`'s H4/H14/H19 read the UNION of body + ALL comments (since PR #10075/#10403 — H4's own header names this card as the ask it discharges), reproduced by running the shipped predicates over real card bytes (a `Blocked-by:` line present only in a NON-latest comment is found and resolved; the live anchor #9857 prints "read from body OR comment" on every H19 row), and the shipped self-test's 1058 cases pass. The census claim that the scan is body-only was false against origin/main.

The one real defect in this territory runs the opposite way — a stale BODY line gates the comment channel off for the liveness read (`needsBlockedByComments()`), publishing false unlock candidates — and that is owned, ruled (option A), and re-dispatched on #11747; it is a different mechanism than this card's ask and does not reopen it.
